\subsection{Reference DAC}\label{ss:dacr2r12}

Two cells produce a channel's reference potential: \texttt{anatop\_pixel\_dacR2R12}, a
12-bit voltage-mode R-2R DAC, and \texttt{anatop\_pixel\_dac\_psu}, the supply block that
feeds it. All data in this section is schematic-level, with no extracted parasitics;
layout and extracted views exist for both cells and have not been simulated.

The ladder is drawn in Figure~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-ladder}. Its terminals are
\texttt{A<11:0>}, \texttt{En} and \texttt{Out}; the supply arrives by inherited
connection and netlists as \texttt{inh\_vdd}/\texttt{inh\_vss}, so there is no supply pin
on the symbol. Each code bit is gated through an \texttt{AND2X8MA10TH} whose output high
level \emph{is} the ladder reference, so whatever drives \texttt{inh\_vdd} sets full
scale directly. Every element of the ladder is the same unit resistor --- \(R\) is two
units in series, \(2R\) four --- which makes the binary weighting a ratio of identical
devices and the converter's linearity a matching property rather than a design margin.
A nodal solve of the transcribed network gives \(V_{\mathrm{out}}/V_{\mathrm{ref}} =
D/4096\) exactly at every code, so none of the nonlinearity reported below is the ratio
design.

Three testbench views drive the two cells. \texttt{DacTB} puts the DAC on an ideal
\SI{2.5}{\volt} rail and measures the ladder alone. \texttt{DacPSUTB} exercises the
supply block by itself against a current load. \texttt{DacWPSUTB} runs both together,
the DAC's inherited supply resolved to \texttt{VddDac} by a \texttt{netSet} property, and
is the block as delivered.

Coverage is five corner points --- the typical statistical point and the ff, fs, sf and
ss skew corners --- and a 200-sample Monte Carlo run varying process and mismatch
together. Temperature is \SI{25}{\celsius} on both DAC benches throughout; the four
supply-block benches run at \SI{27}{\celsius} at the typical point and \SI{25}{\celsius}
at the skew corners. The two DAC benches carry tightened solver tolerances
(\texttt{reltol}~=~\num{1e-6}, \texttt{vabstol}~=~\num{1e-9},
\texttt{iabstol}~=~\num{1e-15}): the LSB through the supply block is \SI{529}{\micro\volt}
and the ADE defaults permit several LSB of error per DC solve, of which DNL is a
difference.

Two defects dominate this section and they are independent. The ladder is
matching-limited and fails its own linearity limits on an ideal rail
(Section~\ref{sss:dacr2r12-mc}). Separately, the supply block modulates the reference by
\SI{25.8}{\milli\volt} peak to peak across the code range against a quarter-LSB budget of
\SI{133}{\micro\volt} (Section~\ref{sss:dacr2r12-supply}). The second is in the corner
data, at \SIrange{25.7}{29.6}{\milli\volt} at every one of the five points; the first is
not, and cannot be, because a process corner moves every ladder resistor together.
